But #426 (David's UsageBench LSP-parity case) deliberately pinned that behavior with a hard-won test expecting `HandlerAlias` to go to `ConsoleHandler`. David's later #2429 rule says navigation follows the selected token's own binding.

Two things you should know about:
- **Master was failing its all-features lint.** My earlier #4733 and another PR landed separately and left a match incomplete. #4813 applies the fix from David's draft #4676, unchanged and credited to him, and I left him a note.
- **Tests already failing on master:** 9 scheduled-only Rust usage tests and 13 cross-language goldens. None of them come from this work.

**Needs you:**
1. **C++ grammar 0.23.6 (#4407):** merged and tagged on the fork, but crates.io has no Trusted Publishing set up for `BrokkAi/tree-sitter-cpp` (David published 0.23.5 by hand). A crate owner needs to set that up or publish it. The Bifrost side is ready on the pushed branch `4407-cpp-linkage-guard-markers`. Note that the first fork PR broke ordinary `#ifdef __cplusplus` blocks; I caught that with a real-corpus comparison and replaced it.
2. **Mjolnir:** the installed `mj-worker` doesn't match the controller build, so I couldn't start or resume sub-agents for the second half of the session and did that work myself. Reinstalling the worker fixes it.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Bifrost's cache key for a language hashes the grammar's node kinds and field names, not its parse tables. A grammar fix that only changes parsing therefore needs a manual cache-key bump, or stale parses survive.
- Reversing a navigation rule touches far more tests than the code change suggests. Many tests had used "navigation lands on the target type" as a stand-in for "the alias resolves correctly". Each one needed its real purpose kept, either through usage lookups or by navigating on the alias's right-hand side.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I created #4820 (https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/issues/4820), assigned it to David, and labelled it `escalated`.

The ticket explains:
- **Why it's blocked:** the publish workflow fails with "No Trusted Publishing config found for repository `BrokkAi/tree-sitter-cpp`". The JavaScript, C# and TypeScript grammar crates publish this way. David published C++ 0.23.5 by hand, so that crate was never set up for Trusted Publishing.
- **What he needs to do, either:**
  - set up Trusted Publishing on crates.io for repository `BrokkAi/tree-sitter-cpp`, workflow `publish.yml`, environment `release`, then rerun the workflow with `release_ref=v0.23.6`. This is the preferred option because later releases then publish automatically;
  - or publish 0.23.6 by hand from tag `v0.23.6`.
- **What 0.23.6 contains:** the split `extern "C"` guard fix (#4407). Across 17,679 real C/C++ files, 46 that failed to parse now parse and none that parsed before fail. It also notes the first attempt that was closed because it broke ordinary `#ifdef __cplusplus` blocks.
- **What happens after publication:** the Bifrost side is ready on the pushed branch `4407-cpp-linkage-guard-markers`. It needs a version bump in three `Cargo.toml` files plus `cargo update`, then a PR.

I also linked #4820 from #4407. Crates.io still shows 0.23.5 as the latest version.
